lessons.title: Create the instance on purpose
lessons.why: The instance is the tenancy boundary for users, flows, and numbers. An accidental second instance splits reports and identity.
paras: You choose identity at creation: Connect-stored users or SAML 2.0. You choose whether the instance places and receives calls, and where recordings and reports go. Changing identity later is a project, not a toggle.
The admin URL and the CCP live on the instance alias under my.connect.aws. Write the alias down. Firewalls and SAML ACS URLs depend on it.
points: Default concurrent calls: 10. Request more before a pilot that is larger than a team.
Storage choices can be updated, but existing objects do not move themselves.
Two instances per Region is the starting quota.
CloudTrail records the control-plane calls. Turn it on in the account, not inside the flow.
lessons.mistake: Creating a production instance in the wrong Region because the console opened there.

lessons.title: SAML attributes that make a user real
lessons.why: A successful SAML login that lands without a routing profile is a user who cannot take a contact.
paras: Map the role, the security profile, and the routing profile from the assertion. Hierarchy is optional and easy to get wrong if your IdP sends a display name and Connect expects the configured group.
IAM Identity Center is a reasonable IdP. It still federates with SAML. Global Resiliency adds a Regional sign-in endpoint. The CCP allow list includes it only when you have onboarded.
points: Test with one user and one profile before you federate the whole center.
Role session name problems show up as opaque access errors. Read the IdP logs and the Connect login error together.
Do not create a parallel local admin and forget it when people leave.
The replica instance needs the same identity story or failover signs nobody in.
lessons.mistake: Declaring SAML done because the IdP returned a success code.

lessons.title: CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform
lessons.why: Clicking the console does not review. A stack does.
paras: The resource types you will actually diff are AWS::Connect::Instance, ContactFlow, ContactFlowModule, HoursOfOperation, Queue, RoutingProfile, User, SecurityProfile, PhoneNumber, QuickConnect, Rule, and TrafficDistributionGroup. Flow content is flow-language JSON.

Terraform mirrors the important ones, including aws_connect_lambda_function_association and aws_connect_bot_association. Association resources are how code attaches Lambda and Lex. The flow still has to reference them.
points: CDK uses the same CloudFormation types.
Phone number resources can fail for quota reasons the template cannot see.
Do not put production flow JSON only in a laptop. The JSON is the source of truth the designer also edits, so pick one writer.
aws-samples and amazon-connect/amazon-connect-streams are the public code to read, not to paste into production unchanged.
lessons.mistake: Exporting a flow once and calling the export a pipeline.

lessons.title: Prompts, statuses, and the small quotas
lessons.why: The limits that surprise people are the ones marked not adjustable.
paras: You get 500 prompts, 50 agent statuses, and 100 security profiles to start. Status count cannot be raised. A status per team, per language, and per campaign will hit 50.
Prompts stored in S3 are called out as not fully replicated by Global Resiliency the way built-in prompts are. Say that in the failover test.
points: Name prompts for the flow that uses them.
Custom statuses feed WFM only if the WFM mapping knows the name.
Reports: 2000 per instance, and every saved personal report counts.
User hierarchy groups: 500 across all levels.
lessons.mistake: Creating a status called Lunch-Team-A through Lunch-Team-Z.
